newsitem.title: USA: Jury asked to find Simpson responsible for deaths.
newsitem.headline: Jury asked to find Simpson responsible for deaths.

text.p: A plaintiffs' attorney in O.J. Simpson's civil trial implored jurors on Monday to find him responsible for the deaths of his ex-wife, Nicole Brown Simpson, and her friend, saying, "One blood drop is enough; one shoeprint is enough."
The jury was expected to begin deliberations on Tuesday afternoon, when closing statements -- which have dragged on longer than expected -- were scheduled to end in the four-month-old trial.

Daniel Petrocelli, who represents the family of murder victim Ronald Goldman, was due to wind up rebuttal arguments, after which Judge Hiroshi Fujisaki was to give legal instructions to the jury before handing it the case.
During Monday's session, Petrocelli pointed out that Simpson's blood was found at the murder scene and the blood of Goldman and Simpson's ex-wife were found in the former football star's Ford Bronco.

Simpson was acquitted of the June 12, 1994, murders in a 1995 criminal trial. He is now battling a wrongful-death civil lawsuit brought by the families of the victims, who are seeking substantial damages.
Petrocelli, in countering arguments by Simpson's defence team that there was a police conspiracy to frame him in the murders, said that was "absolutely false."
"It's nonsense; it's absurd," he said of the claim made by Robert Baker, Simpson's lead defence attorney, that blood from the victims and from Simpson had been planted by detectives in the case.
"The whole planting and conspiracy theory is a big lie," Petrocelli added.

He said Simpson's defence team had no reasonable answer for the 31 photographs of Simpson apparently wearing Italian designer Bruno Magli shoes at a 1993 Buffalo Bills football game just months before the murder.

"How do you fake 31 photographs months and months before the murders were committed, when you don't even know Nicole and Ron Goldman are going to be murdered?" he asked. An expert FBI witness testified during the trial that bloody shoeprints at the murder scene were left by similar Bruno Magli shoes.
Baker last week told the jury in relation to the evidence planting theory, "If you can't trust the messenger, you can't trust the message."
Petrocelli countered on Monday by telling the jury, "The messenger you can't trust in this case ... is O.J. Simpson, who has lied and lied and lied."
Earlier on Monday, Baker argued that Nicole Brown Simpson and Goldman were killed by two people and that police framed the former athlete, actor and TV pitchman for the murders.

Pointing to high-profile cases that he said had embarrassed both the Los Angeles Police Department and the district attorney's office through their failure to get convictions, Baker said, "They were going to win this one, they were going to get O.J. Simpson."

Winding up defence closing arguments, Baker told the jury, "You can't give Fred Goldman his son back but you can give back Mr. Simpson his life ... and give Justin and Sydney their dad back." Justin and Sydney are Simpson's young children from his marriage to Nicole Brown Simpson.
Baker said the main culprit in the conspiracy to frame Simpson was former detective Mark Fuhrman, whom he referred to as "the rogue Fuhrman."

Fuhrman, who said he found a bloody glove on Simpson's estate the morning after the murders, was discredited at the criminal trial when defence lawyers showed he was lying when he said he had not used the racial slur "nigger" anytime in the last 10 years.
Fuhrman subsequently pleaded no contest to a single charge of perjury and was fined and placed on probation. He did not testify in the civil trial.
